assigned.title: Playback session route refuses an oversized request body
assigned.acceptance: The production playback-session route refuses a request body above a declared bound before parsing it, and the refusal carries a reason code that exists in the contract. TODAY IT READS AN UNBOUNDED BODY: apps/web/src/app/api/v1/playback/session/playback-session-implementation.ts reads the body with no cap while the development-only resolve scaffold beside it caps one, so the production path is the weaker of the two. This is a task rather than a line in PL-0702 because the fix cannot be made honestly inside that task's surface: there is no reason code for an oversized body, adding one changes API behaviour, and invariant 5 requires docs/API_CONTRACTS.md to change first or deliberately alongside. Required: the bound is a named constant with the reason for its value, not a magic number; the reason code is added to the contract and to docs/API_CONTRACTS.md in the same change; the refusal happens BEFORE the body is buffered, because a cap enforced after reading the whole body does not bound memory; a regression drives a body over the bound through the real route and observes the refusal, and a second drives one just under it and observes normal handling, since a cap that refuses everything is indistinguishable from an outage. Out of scope: the candidate-id bound, which is PL-0708, and any change to what a well-formed request means.

unit.evidence: npx turbo run test --force, exit 0, 17 of 17, 0 cached, 2409 passed across the wave. RED, with handler.ts and contract.ts restored to HEAD and the new tests kept: 5 failed 9 passed, 'expected undefined to be 16384' (no named bound exists), 'expected 200 to be 413' three times -- a 16 KiB body granted, a LYING content-length of 42 granted, and a streamed body with NO content-length granted -- and 'expected 503 to be 413' where the implementation was reached. Desktop suite: 4 failed 17 passed, 'boundRequestBody is not a function'. GREEN: 5 files, 127 passed. THE HEADER IS NOT THE BOUND, which is the part worth reading: chunked encoding carries no content-length and the header is trivially forged, so content-length is consulted only to refuse EARLIER, and the actual control is a metered read of request.body that stops the instant the running total exceeds the cap and cancels the reader on every exit path -- peak memory is the bound plus one chunk whatever the header claimed. The gate consumes the stream and replays the bounded bytes as a new Request so the seam keeps its shape; a test asserts the replay is byte-for-byte. The outage guard -- a body just under the bound returning 200 granted -- PASSED at HEAD, correctly, because it is not a defect probe. Fixtures are sized from a local literal rather than from the constant under test, because a fixture sized from MAX_REQUEST_BODY_BYTES degenerates to a tiny body on a tree where the constant does not exist, which would have made the red observation dishonest; a separate test ties the literal to the exported constant. Both build targets are covered by one cap in handler.ts, and the desktop test asserts 413 with remote.calls EMPTY, so an oversized body is never relayed to our own backend.

recommended.title: Provider outbound HTTP resolves, classifies and pins its destination
recommended.acceptance: Provider outbound HTTP adopts the existing @liberty/media-inspection resolve-and-pin control (authoriseFetchTarget / nodePinnedFetch) instead of classifying host literals. Required, and each clause is a separate way host-literal checking fails: DNS resolution happens BEFORE the outbound connection; EVERY resolved address is classified, not just the first; the request is refused if ANY resolved address is private, loopback, link-local or reserved, unless an explicitly permitted local-only path applies; the connection is PINNED to the approved resolved address, so DNS rebinding cannot change the destination between the check and the connect; redirects repeat resolution, classification and pinning PER HOP; and TLS hostname verification and SNI are not regressed -- pinning to an address must still present and verify the name. Tests are required for public-name-to-private-IP, DNS rebinding, mixed public/private answer sets, and translation-prefix cases. WHY THIS IS P0 AND WHY IT IS FILED NOW: F1, F7 and F8 are three defects of ONE SHAPE in one function -- a host spelling the string comparisons did not anticipate, each reading as public, none findable by reading. A check that compares a string against literals is only ever as complete as the list of spellings whoever wrote it thought of. Resolve-and-pin classifies the address a resolver returned, which has one spelling.
